findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects are stored unencrypted at rest by default (only SSE-S3 default may apply depending on account settings, but no explicit encryption or KMS enforcement is configured), and no ACL/public access block is defined, leaving the bucket's access posture ambiguous and potentially defaulting to less restrictive settings.
The bucket does not specify an ACL or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so it could be left with permissive default access, exposing potentially sensitive reports data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger/financial exports, meaning sensitive financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest, increasing risk if the bucket contents are exposed or the storage layer is compromised.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbooks (potentially containing sensitive operational/security details) unencrypted at rest.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; if this were intended to be 'log-delivery-write', it grants broad write/read-acp permissions to the log delivery group, which combined with a typo could cause unpredictable access control behavior or apply failures that mask a permissive configuration. This bucket stores audit logs and should have tightly scoped access.

The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and it inherits the bucket's lack of default encryption, meaning this vendor roster file (potentially containing PII/business data) is stored unencrypted.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be permanently deleted via a single terraform destroy/apply operation without additional safeguards, risking irreversible data loss of report data.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows deletion of compliance/audit logs, undermining tamper-resistance and non-repudiation guarantees expected of an audit trail.
